feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: You'd expect homeowners to save their stuff. Federal policy pays them to leave it
entry.summary: NPR dug into the upside-down world of FEMA flood insurance in coastal areas, and found many homeowners have no financial choice but to let their homes collapse.

entry.title: Committee investigating Epstein holds billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress
entry.summary: Billionaire investor Leon Black refused to appear before the committee investigating convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein for a deposition. Now it's up to the Department of Justice whether to pursue criminal charges.

entry.title: The 'burnerverse' exploiting young women in college
entry.summary: Wired reporter EJ Dickson speaks with NPR's Juana Summers about an online community that targets and harasses young women with their own nonconsensual, sexually explicit images.

entry.title: DOJ charges Russian agents with plotting attacks, including in the U.S.
entry.summary: The indictment says the defendants belong to a network that "is one arm of the Russian Federation's apparatus used to carry out external attacks" worldwide.

entry.title: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
entry.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

entry.title: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
entry.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

entry.title: Why Steve Bannon sided with Sanders, not Trump, on AI
entry.summary: Where does Steve Bannon fit in the debate over regulating or slowing AI? He tells Morning Edition where he breaks with Trump and what he thinks Washington should do.

entry.title: The price tag for the Iran war has hit over $30B, reports say
entry.summary: Two new reports detail the damage the Iran war has caused to U.S. bases and the rising cost of the war, which has hit over $30 billion.

entry.title: U.S. acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space
entry.summary: The remarkable revelation comes after previous warnings about countries such as Russia possibly weaponizing a global frontier long agreed in treaties to be used for only peaceful purposes.

entry.title: 3 people killed when news helicopter crashes while covering LA bus accident
entry.summary: A news helicopter used by NBC and Telemundo crashed in a Los Angeles neighborhood on Tuesday, killing at least three people while reporters were covering the nearby crash of an SUV and a city bus.
